title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
description: “Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!” — “Nobody believes a liar!”
subtitle: An Aesop’s fable • A bedtime tale about a bored shepherd boy, two false alarms, and why nobody believes a liar.

cover.alt: The shepherd boy laughs at the furious villagers after his false wolf alarm.

blocks.html: There once was a shepherd boy who was bored as he sat on the hillside watching the village sheep.

blocks.alt: A bored shepherd boy sits on a sunny hillside watching his flock of white sheep graze, the village in the valley below.
blocks.caption: A shepherd boy, bored on the hillside.

blocks.html: It was rather lonely for him all day, so he played on his shepherd's pipe, and thought upon a plan by which he could get a little company and some excitement.

blocks.alt: The shepherd boy plays his pipe on the grassy hillside, his sheepdog beside him, looking lonely and restless.
blocks.caption: Lonely and restless, he hatches a plan.

blocks.html: To amuse himself he took a great breath and sang out...

🧒 The Boy
“Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!”

blocks.alt: The mischievous boy cups his hands around his mouth, about to shout from the hillside with a naughty grin.
blocks.caption: “Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!”

blocks.html: The villagers came running up the hill to help the boy drive the wolf away. But when they arrived at the top of the hill, they found no wolf.

blocks.alt: Villagers rush up the winding hillside path in alarm, carrying pitchforks and sticks toward the pasture.
blocks.caption: The villagers come running — but there is no wolf.

blocks.html: The boy laughed at the sight of their angry faces.

🧑‍🌾 The Villagers
“Don't cry 'wolf', shepherd boy, when there's no wolf!” — They went grumbling back down the hill.

blocks.alt: The boy doubles over laughing at the furious villagers, who shake their fists — there is no wolf anywhere.
blocks.caption: The boy laughs at their angry faces.

blocks.html: The boy felt a little ashamed, but not for long. For the joke had been such fun, he could think of nothing else all day.

blocks.alt: A stern village woman raises her finger to scold the sheepish boy while other villagers walk grumbling back down the path.
blocks.caption: A stern warning — but the joke was too much fun.

blocks.html: Later, the boy sang out again, "Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!" To his naughty delight, he watched the villagers run up the hill to help him drive the wolf away.

blocks.alt: The boy grins gleefully, cupping his hands to shout toward the village a second time, his sheep grazing peacefully behind him.
blocks.caption: He cries wolf a second time.

blocks.html: When the villagers saw no wolf they sternly said, "Save your frightened song for when there is really something wrong! Don't cry 'wolf' when there is NO wolf!" But the boy just grinned and watched them go grumbling down the hill once more.

blocks.alt: Angry villagers trudge grumbling back down the path while the boy waves mockingly from the hill.
blocks.caption: Grumbling down the hill once more.

blocks.html: That evening the boy promised himself he would never play the trick again. But a promise made to yourself is easy to forget.

blocks.alt: A stern grey-bearded villager points a warning finger at the cheeky, unrepentant boy as evening light softens the pasture.
blocks.caption: One last warning.

blocks.html: Later, he saw a REAL wolf prowling about his flock, come out from the dark forest.

blocks.alt: A real grey wolf prowls low out of the dark forest edge toward the grazing sheep; the boy turns in alarm in the distance.
blocks.caption: This time the wolf is REAL.

blocks.html: Alarmed, he leaped to his feet and sang out as loudly as he could, "Wolf! Wolf!"

blocks.alt: The terrified boy leaps up shouting toward the village as the wolf prowls among the scattering sheep.
blocks.caption: He cries for help — and means it this time.

blocks.html: But the villagers thought he was trying to fool them again, and so they didn't come. "He cannot fool us again," they said, and went on with their work.

blocks.alt: In the village, people calmly go about their evening business, deliberately ignoring the distant cry; a tiny figure shouts unheard on the hill.
blocks.caption: “He cannot fool us again.”

blocks.html: At sunset, everyone wondered why the shepherd boy hadn't returned to the village with their sheep. They went up the hill to find the boy.

blocks.alt: At sunset the villagers gather in the square with worried faces, the old man pointing up the hill where the boy has not returned.
blocks.caption: Why hasn't the boy come home?

blocks.html:
😢 The Boy
“There really was a wolf here! The flock has scattered! I cried out, 'Wolf!' Why didn't you come?”

blocks.alt: At dusk, villagers with lanterns find the weeping boy sitting alone among trampled grass, his sheep scattered and huddled far away.
blocks.caption: “Why didn't you come?”

blocks.html: An old man tried to comfort the boy as they walked back to the village. "We'll help you look for the lost sheep in the morning," he said, putting his arm around the youth. And that is the end of the tale.

🧓 The Wise Old Man
“Nobody believes a liar, even when he is telling the truth!”

blocks.alt: The kind old man puts a comforting arm around the tearful boy as they walk back down to the village at dusk.
blocks.caption: “Nobody believes a liar, even when he is telling the truth!”

discussionHtml:
💭 Bedtime Chat

What should the boy have done instead of crying “wolf” for fun?

🗣️ Tell the Truth Lying for fun cost the boy his flock. Telling the truth, even when it’s boring, keeps people’s trust — and trust is hard to win back.
🎺 Find a Better Game The boy was bored, and boredom made him mischievous. When you’re bored, find a real game to play — like the boy’s pipe — instead of tricking people.
